courseTitle: Swedish for YKI: A1 to B1
description: Words and sentences for the YKI exam: 84 short daily lessons from A1 to B1, and 7 B1 exam topics.

levels.title: A1 Foundations
levels.description: Build survival Swedish for greetings, daily routines, shopping, transport, health, and short social interaction.
objectives: Understand very common words and fixed phrases in slow, clear Swedish.
Introduce yourself and manage routine service situations.
Write short messages, forms, and simple personal texts.

lessons.title: Places in town and simple directions
Body, pain, and simple health talk
Simple past: yesterday and last weekend

levels.title: A2 Everyday Independence
levels.description: Extend Swedish toward independent everyday use with longer sentences, past and future time, services, and practical writing.
objectives: Handle predictable situations at work, school, healthcare, and public services.
Describe plans, experiences, and problems with short connected speech.
Read and write common notices, emails, and simple opinion texts.

lessons.title: Comparison, preference, and choosing between options
Moving, furniture, and practical home problems
Job search, CV basics, and applications
Public services, forms, and identity details
Past tense stories and sequencing events
Reading notices, instructions, and warning signs
Email structure, polite requests, and replies
Rules, habits, and what people should do
News basics and short spoken summaries
Longer speaking turns and discourse markers
A2 review, production check, and B1 bridge

levels.title: B1 YKI Readiness
levels.description: Train the vocabulary, grammar control, and production stamina needed for late-August YKI-style tasks.
objectives: Follow the main point of everyday Swedish in speech and writing.
Explain opinions, reasons, experiences, and practical problems in connected Swedish.
Simulate reading, listening, speaking, and writing tasks under time pressure.

lessons.title: Healthcare, wellbeing, and longer symptom descriptions
Work rights, responsibilities, and workplace culture
Neighbour issues, housing contracts, and compromise
Environment, local issues, and public debate
Culture, traditions, and comparison across countries
Planning a project and dividing tasks
Narrating events in order with detail
Formal phone calls and spoken service interaction
Formal emails, requests, and follow-up writing
Reading longer texts and extracting the main argument
Listening for gist, detail, and speaker intention
Opinion writing with structure and support
Listening mock strategies and recovery tactics
Reading mock strategies and time management
Speaking mock 1: familiar life and practical topics
Speaking mock 2: opinions, comparison, and discussion
Writing mock: practical message plus opinion text
Integrated mock debrief and targeted repair
Final consolidation and late-August test week

days.title: Greetings, alphabet, and polite openings
days.goal: Recognize Swedish sounds and manage the first 30 seconds of a conversation.

vocabulary.exampleEnglish: Thank you very much for the help.

vocabulary.english: you are welcome / here you go
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: Here you go, here is your coffee.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: God morgon, hur mår du idag?
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: Good morning, how are you today?

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Jag köper ett kylskåp i Kina.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I am buying a fridge in China.

tips: When talking about how you feel, Swedish prefers “Jag mår bra” instead of “Jag är bra.”
Swedish often says “Jag mår bra” for “I am fine.” Literally it means “I feel well,” so do not replace it with “Jag är bra.”
A short answer is common in everyday speech: “Bra, tack.” You can also continue with “Och du?” to keep the conversation going.

lines.english: I am fine, thanks. And you?

lines.english: Fine too. See you later.

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Goodbye!

days.title: Name, country, and language
days.goal: Introduce yourself and say where you are from and which languages you speak.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Jag talar engelska och lite svenska.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I speak English and a little Swedish.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Jag kommer från Indien. Och du?
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I come from India. And you?

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Jag talar engelska och lite svenska.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I speak English and a little Swedish.

tips: Use “Jag heter ...” for your name and “Jag kommer från ...” or “Jag bor i ...” for origin and residence.
“Jag heter” means “my name is.” To say where you are from, use “Jag kommer från ...” or “Jag är från ...” in simple beginner speech.
Use “Jag bor i ...” for the place where you live now. A beginner self-introduction can combine all three patterns: name, country, and city.

lines.speaker: A
lines.swedish: Hej, jag heter Lina. Vad heter du?
lines.english: Hi, my name is Lina. What is your name?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: My name is Ravi.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Where are you from?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Jag kommer från Indien men jag bor i Finland.
lines.english: I come from India but I live in Finland.

dialogues.title: Saying your name and where you are from

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Hi! My name is Anna.

lines.speaker: B

lines.english: I come from Sweden and I live in Uppsala.

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Nice to meet you!

days.title: Classroom survival Swedish
days.goal: Ask for repetition, clarification, and help during study situations.

vocabulary.exampleEnglish: What does that mean in Swedish?
I need help with the exercise.
Excuse me, can you help me?
Can you speak more slowly, please?

vocabulary.english: how do you say ... in Swedish?
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: How do you say “table” in Swedish?
Excuse me, I do not really understand.

tips: “Kan du ...?” is the most useful polite request frame at beginner level. Add “tack” to soften it.
“Kan du ...?” means “Can you ...?” and is a useful polite frame for requests. “Jag förstår inte” means “I do not understand.”
When you ask about language, “på svenska” means “in Swedish” and “på engelska” means “in English.”

lines.speaker: Lärare
lines.english: Do you understand the text?

lines.speaker: Student
lines.english: Not completely. Can you repeat?

lines.speaker: Lärare
lines.english: Yes, of course.

lines.speaker: Student
lines.english: Thanks. What does “assignment” mean?

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Do you understand?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Not really. Can you repeat?

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Of course.

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Thanks! What does “från” mean?

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: It means “from”.

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Bra, tack. Kan du tala långsammare också?
lines.english: Good, thanks. Can you speak more slowly too?

days.title: Numbers, age, and contact details
days.goal: Use numbers in everyday personal information tasks.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Min adress är enkel att hitta.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: My address is easy to find.
The bus leaves in fifteen minutes.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Kan du säga sista siffran igen?
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: Can you say the last digit again?

tips: For age, use “Jag är ... år.” For phone numbers, chunk digits in pairs to sound more natural.
To say your age, Swedish uses “Jag är ... år.” The word “år” means “years old” in this context.
Phone numbers are usually read digit by digit. Practice them slowly first and then at a more natural speed.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: How old are you?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: I am thirty-four years old.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: And what is your phone number?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Det är noll fyrtio, tjugoett, sextioåtta, nittiotre.
lines.english: It is zero forty, twenty-one, sixty-eight, ninety-three.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: How old are you?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: I am thirty years old.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: What is your phone number?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: It starts with zero seven.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Can you say the rest slowly?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Ja: noll sju, tre två, fem nio.
lines.english: Yes: zero seven, three two, five nine.

rows.Swedish: femton, sexton, sjutton, arton, nitton, tjugo

days.title: Family, pronouns, and close relations
days.goal: Talk about your family and use the most common personal pronouns.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Min familj bor i två länder.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: My family lives in two countries.

tips: Use the subject pronouns “jag, du, han, hon, vi, ni, de”. In speech, “dom” is common for “de”.
After “Jag talar ...” use the language name, for example “Jag talar engelska.” Nationalities often change form depending on gender and number, so start by recognizing them.
A simple beginner pattern is: country with “kommer från”, language with “talar”, and nationality with “är”.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Do you have siblings?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Ja, jag har en syster och en bror.
lines.english: Yes, I have one sister and one brother.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Where do they live?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: They live in Stockholm.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Which language do you speak?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Jag talar engelska och lite svenska.
lines.english: I speak English and a little Swedish.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Where are you from?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: I come from India.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Do you also speak Hindi?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Ja, och jag lär mig svenska.
lines.english: Yes, and I am learning Swedish.

days.title: Home, rooms, and basic furniture
days.goal: Describe where you live and name the main rooms and objects at home.

vocabulary.exampleEnglish: The kitchen is small but bright.
The table is in the living room.

tips: Swedish nouns need an article. Start noticing “en” and “ett” together with the noun, not as separate facts.
Swedish subject pronouns usually stay before the verb in simple statements: “Jag bor här.” “Hon studerar.”

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Where do you live?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Jag bor i en liten lägenhet nära centrum.
lines.english: I live in a small apartment near the center.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Do you have your own kitchen?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Yes, and a quiet bedroom.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Do you live here?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Yes, I live here.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: And your friends?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: They also live here.

days.title: Daily routines and present tense
days.goal: Talk about a normal day using high-frequency present-tense verbs.

vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I wake up at six o’clock.

tips: In present tense, many Swedish verbs end in “-r”: “jag jobbar”, “jag studerar”, “jag äter”.
The present form is “är” for all persons: jag är, du är, vi är. Swedish does not change it like English does with am / is / are.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: When do you wake up on weekdays?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Jag vaknar klockan sex och jag arbetar från åtta.
lines.english: I wake up at six and I work from eight.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Do you study Swedish in the evening?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Yes, I study after dinner.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Are you a student?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Yes, I am a student.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Are you tired today?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: A little, but I am fine.

days.title: Time, weekdays, and appointments
days.goal: Tell the time and talk about schedules and simple appointments.

vocabulary.exampleEnglish: The meeting starts at three o’clock.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Jag har en tid hos läkaren.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I have an appointment with the doctor.

tips: Use “klockan” with clock times. For appointments, combine time with day: “på tisdag klockan tre”.
A safe beginner pattern is subject + verb + object/place/time: “Jag läser svenska hemma.” Keep that pattern until it feels automatic.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: When does the course start?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: On Tuesday at nine o’clock.

lines.speaker: A
lines.swedish: Har du en tid hos läkaren också?
lines.english: Do you also have an appointment with the doctor?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Yes, on Thursday afternoon.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: What do you do every day?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: I study Swedish at home.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Do you also work?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Yes, I work in town.

days.title: Food, drinks, and breakfast talk
days.goal: Name everyday food and say what you eat and drink.

vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I drink coffee in the morning.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Hon vill ha te utan socker.

vocabulary.exampleEnglish: Is there milk in the fridge?
Breakfast is my most important meal.
The milk is out of stock.

tips: After “jag vill ha” use the noun directly: “Jag vill ha kaffe”, “Jag vill ha en smörgås.”
Common question words are “vad” (what), “vem” (who), and “var” (where). In simple questions the verb usually comes before the subject.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: What do you eat for breakfast?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Jag äter bröd och dricker kaffe.
lines.english: I eat bread and drink coffee.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Do you take milk in the coffee?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Yes, a little milk.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: What is your name?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: My name is Lina.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Where do you live?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: I live in Uppsala.

days.title: Grocery shopping basics
days.goal: Ask for items, quantities, and prices in a supermarket.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Jag vill ha ett kilo potatis.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I want one kilo of potatoes.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Försök svara utan att titta i boken.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: Try to answer without looking in the book.

tips: For questions in shops, keep the verb in second position: “Var finns ...?”, “Hur mycket kostar ...?”
Review days matter because A1 progress comes from reusing the same structures until they become quick and familiar.

lines.speaker: Kund
lines.english: Excuse me, where is the rice?

lines.speaker: Personal
lines.english: It is on shelf four.

lines.speaker: Kund
lines.english: And how much do the apples cost?

lines.speaker: Personal
lines.english: Three euros per kilo.

lines.speaker: A
lines.swedish: Hej! Jag heter Sara. Vad heter du?
lines.english: Hi! My name is Sara. What is your name?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Jag heter Amir. Jag kommer från Iran.
lines.english: My name is Amir. I come from Iran.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Where do you live now?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Jag bor i Stockholm och jag talar lite svenska.
lines.english: I live in Stockholm and I speak a little Swedish.

days.title: Cafe and restaurant phrases
days.goal: Order politely and talk about simple preferences in a cafe or restaurant.

vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I have a partner who lives separately.

tips: Use modal verbs for polite requests: “Jag skulle vilja ha ...” sounds softer than only “Jag vill ha ...”.
To ask “Do you have ...?” use “Har du ...?” and answer with “Ja, jag har ...” or “Nej, jag har inte ...”.

lines.speaker: Servitör
lines.english: Hi, what would you like to order?

lines.speaker: Gäst
lines.swedish: Jag skulle vilja ha en soppa och kaffe utan mjölk.
lines.english: I would like a soup and coffee without milk.

lines.speaker: Servitör
lines.english: Of course. Anything else?

lines.speaker: Gäst
lines.swedish: Nej tack. Kan jag få notan senare?
lines.english: No thanks. Can I get the bill later?

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Do you have siblings?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Yes, I have a sister.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Where does your family live?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: My family lives in Delhi.

days.title: Transport, tickets, and commuting
days.goal: Use basic Swedish for buses, trains, and everyday commuting.

vocabulary.exampleEnglish: The bus leaves in five minutes.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Jag behöver en biljett till Åbo.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I need a ticket to Turku.
The train is ten minutes delayed.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Hennes ord kan förstöra mitt äktenskap.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: Her words can ruin my marriage.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Efter detta städar Nils bara sitt eget skrivbord.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: After that, Nils only cleans his own desk.

tips: Use “med” for transport mode: “Jag åker med buss”, “Jag kommer med tåg.”
Common possessives are “min / mitt / mina” for my and “din / ditt / dina” for your. At this stage, recognize the forms and use common chunks like “min familj”.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: When does the bus to the center leave?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Om sju minuter från hållplats tre.
lines.english: In seven minutes from stop three.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Do I need to buy a ticket here?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Yes, or in the app.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Is that your book?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Yes, it is my book.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Who is he?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: He is her brother.

days.title: Places in town and simple directions
days.goal: Find places and ask where things are in town.

vocabulary.exampleEnglish: The hospital is near the station.
Turn left at the traffic light.
She is a manager at the company.

tips: Use “var ligger ...?” for location and “gå / sväng / fortsätt” for basic route instructions.
Use “Jag är ...” for professions in simple introductions and “Jag studerar ...” or “Jag jobbar som ...” for more detail.

dialogues.title: Places in town and simple directions

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Excuse me, where is the bank?

lines.speaker: B

lines.english: Go straight ahead and turn left.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Is it far?

lines.speaker: B

days.title: Weather, seasons, and clothing
days.goal: Talk about weather and choose suitable clothes.
tips: Weather often uses “det”: “Det regnar”, “Det är kallt”, “Det blåser mycket.”
In the present tense, many Swedish verbs end in -r: bor, läser, skriver, talar. Learn them as whole forms first.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: How is the weather today?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Det regnar och det är ganska kallt.
lines.english: It is raining and it is quite cold.

lines.speaker: A
lines.swedish: Då tar jag min varma jacka.
lines.english: Then I will take my warm jacket.

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Good idea.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Do you drink coffee?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Ja, jag dricker kaffe varje morgon.
lines.english: Yes, I drink coffee every morning.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Do you write in Swedish?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Lite grann, jag skriver enkla meningar.
lines.english: A little, I write simple sentences.

days.title: Body, pain, and simple health talk
days.goal: Say what hurts and understand basic health questions.

vocabulary.exampleEnglish: The child has a stomach ache.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Jag tror att jag har feber.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I think I have a fever.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Jag behöver prata med en läkare.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I need to speak with a doctor.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Jag gillar svenska eftersom språket är fint.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I like Swedish because the language is beautiful.

tips: Use “Jag har ont i ...” for pain and “Jag är sjuk” for being ill.
Use “Jag gillar ...” for “I like ...” and “Jag gillar inte ...” for “I do not like ...”. The negation comes after the verb.

dialogues.title: Body, pain, and simple health talk

lines.speaker: Sjukskötare
lines.english: What is the problem?

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.swedish: Jag har ont i huvudet och jag känner mig sjuk.
lines.english: I have a headache and I feel sick.

lines.speaker: Sjukskötare
lines.english: Do you have a fever?

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.english: Yes, a little fever.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Do you like Swedish music?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Yes, I like Swedish music.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Do you like tea?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: No, I do not like tea.

days.title: Work, school, and daily responsibilities
days.goal: Talk about your job, studies, and common daily obligations.

vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I have a lot of work today.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Jag har ett möte klockan två.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I have a meeting at two o’clock.
We have a break after the lesson.

tips: Use present tense for ongoing roles: “Jag arbetar som ...”, “Jag studerar ...”.
When naming food in basic speech, short noun phrases are enough: “en kaffe” is common in cafés, although “en kopp kaffe” is more literal.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: What do you do during the day?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Jag arbetar deltid och jag studerar svenska på kvällen.
lines.english: I work part time and study Swedish in the evening.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Do you have many meetings?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Inte så många, men många uppgifter.
lines.english: Not so many, but many tasks.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: What would you like?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Jag vill ha kaffe och bröd.
lines.english: I would like coffee and bread.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Anything else to drink?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Yes, a glass of water.

days.title: Hobbies, likes, and free time
days.goal: Talk about what you like doing and how you spend your free time.

vocabulary.exampleEnglish: In my free time I read a lot.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Jag tränar tre gånger i veckan.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I exercise three times a week.
I am reading a Swedish book.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Musik hjälper mig att slappna av.
Jag skulle vilja ha en kaffe.

tips: Use “jag gillar att ...” with an infinitive verb: “Jag gillar att läsa”, “Jag gillar att springa.”
A very useful pattern is “Jag skulle vilja ha ...” for a polite “I would like ...”, but “Jag vill ha ...” is acceptable at beginner level.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: What do you do in your free time?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Jag gillar att läsa och träna.
lines.english: I like to read and exercise.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Do you listen to music too?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Yes, every day.

lines.speaker: A
lines.swedish: Hej, vad får det lov att vara?
lines.english: Hello, what would you like?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Jag skulle vilja ha en kaffe utan socker.
lines.english: I would like a coffee without sugar.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Anything else?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Ja, kan jag få notan senare?
lines.english: Yes, can I get the bill later?

days.title: Calendar, months, and dates
days.goal: Use dates, months, and common calendar language.

vocabulary.exampleEnglish: The YKI test is in August.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Jag skriver allt i min kalender.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I write everything in my calendar.
The book is on a table.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Jag skriver allt i ett schema.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I write everything in a schedule.

tips: For dates, learn the fixed patterns: “den tredje juni”, “i augusti”, “på fredag”.
There is no perfect rule for en and ett at A1 level, so memorize common noun phrases like “en bok” and “ett hus.”

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: What date is the course start?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: On the fifth of August.

lines.speaker: A
lines.swedish: Bra, jag skriver det i min kalender.
lines.english: Good, I will write it in my calendar.

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Do it right away.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Is it a book?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Yes, it is a book.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: And over there?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Det är ett bord och en stol.
lines.english: It is a table and a chair.

days.title: Household tasks and chores
days.goal: Talk about cleaning, cooking, and simple home responsibilities.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Andreas köper biljetter på nätet just nu.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: Andreas is buying tickets online right now.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Lena gör två fruktsallader till sina söner.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: Lena is making two fruit salads for her sons.

tips: Use frequency words to make routines clearer: “ofta”, “ibland”, “alltid”, “sällan”.
Swedish plural patterns vary, so begin with high-frequency pairs such as bok / böcker and stol / stolar.

lines.speaker: A
lines.swedish: Vem lagar mat hemma hos er?
lines.english: Who cooks at your home?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: We cook together.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: And who takes out the garbage?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: I usually do that.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: How many books do you have?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: I have many books.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Are there chairs here?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Yes, there are four chairs.

days.title: Simple past: yesterday and last weekend
days.goal: Start talking about completed actions in the past.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Vi gör ett kort rollspel idag.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: We are doing a short roleplay today.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Försök att blanda gamla och nya ord.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: Try to mix old and new words.

tips: A1 Swedish can start with a few common past forms as chunks: “var”, “gjorde”, “åt”, “gick”, “såg”.
Roleplay is useful because it forces you to retrieve language quickly instead of only recognizing it.

dialogues.title: Simple past: yesterday and last weekend

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: What did you do yesterday?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Jag gick till jobbet och jag åt lunch med en vän.
lines.english: I went to work and ate lunch with a friend.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Did you do anything in the evening?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Ja, jag såg en film hemma.
lines.english: Yes, I watched a movie at home.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Shall we practice together?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Yes, ask a question.

lines.speaker: A
lines.swedish: Vad vill du ha på kaféet?
lines.english: What would you like at the café?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Jag skulle vilja ha kaffe och bröd.
lines.english: I would like coffee and bread.

days.title: Plans and near future
days.goal: Talk about tomorrow, next week, and your short-term plans.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Min plan är att träna mer.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: My plan is to exercise more.
I am going to call the doctor.
I work at home on Friday.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Jag hade så mycket att göra i måndags.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I had so much to do last Monday.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: På onsdagar tränar jag alltid på gymmet.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: On Wednesdays I always work out at the gym.

tips: Swedish often uses present tense for the future with a time word: “Imorgon jobbar jag hemma.”
To say “on Monday” Swedish often uses just the day word in context, but “på måndag” means “on Monday / this coming Monday.”

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: What are you going to do tomorrow?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Jag ska arbeta på morgonen och studera senare.
lines.english: I will work in the morning and study later.

lines.speaker: A
lines.swedish: Har du några planer för helgen?
lines.english: Do you have any plans for the weekend?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Yes, I am going to meet friends.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: When do you study Swedish?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Jag studerar på måndag och onsdag.
lines.english: I study on Monday and Wednesday.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: What do you do on Friday?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Jag jobbar och sedan vilar jag på helgen.
lines.english: I work and then I rest on the weekend.

days.title: Messages, invitations, and social replies
days.goal: Write and answer very short social messages in Swedish.

vocabulary.exampleEnglish: Do you want to have coffee tomorrow?

vocabulary.english: we will talk / be in touch
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: We will be in touch later.

tips: Keep messages short and direct. Swedish often drops extra words when the context is obvious.
Dates in Swedish are often said with ordinal-like forms in speech, but at A1 level it is fine to recognize and read simple dates slowly.

lines.speaker: Meddelande 1
lines.english: Hi! Do you want to have coffee tomorrow?

lines.speaker: Meddelande 2
lines.english: Yes, gladly. What time?

lines.speaker: Meddelande 1
lines.english: Five o’clock works well.

lines.speaker: Meddelande 2
lines.english: Perfect, talk later!

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: When is your birthday?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: In May.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: What is the date of the meeting?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: It is on the twelfth of August.

days.title: A1 consolidation and mini mock
days.goal: Review A1 material and combine it into short YKI-style micro tasks.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Dagens övning är kort men viktig.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: Today’s exercise is short but important.
I want to improve the pronunciation.
It is half past two / half to three in Swedish style.
The lesson starts at nine o’clock.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Vad är det för datum idag?

vocabulary.exampleEnglish: The meeting starts at five on the dot.

tips: At A1, speed with basic patterns is more valuable than knowing many isolated rules.
A practical beginner structure is “Klockan är ...” for “The time is ...” and “När börjar ...?” for asking when something starts.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: How does A1 feel now?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Bättre. Jag kan prata lite mer utan att tänka så länge.
lines.english: Better. I can speak a bit more without thinking so long.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: What do you need to practice more?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Times, pronunciation, and longer answers.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: What time is it?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: It is half past two / Swedish half three.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: When does the lesson start?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: It starts at three.

days.title: Describing people, appearance, and personality
days.goal: Use richer adjectives to describe people clearly and politely.

vocabulary.exampleEnglish: The child is a little shy at first.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Vi pratar om personlighet, inte bara utseende.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: We are talking about personality, not only appearance.

tips: Swedish adjectives often change with “ett” nouns and plurals. Begin noticing “snäll”, “snällt”, “snälla”.
To describe routine, combine time words with present verbs: “Jag vaknar klockan sju. Sedan äter jag frukost.”

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: What is your new colleague like?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Hon är vänlig, lugn och väldigt tydlig.
lines.english: She is friendly, calm, and very clear.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Is she also social?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Yes, but not loud.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: When do you wake up?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Jag vaknar klockan sju och äter frukost.
lines.english: I wake up at seven and eat breakfast.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: When do you start work?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: I start work at nine.

days.title: Comparison, preference, and choosing between options
days.goal: Compare alternatives and explain simple preferences.

vocabulary.exampleEnglish: The train is cheaper than the car.
I would rather walk than drive.
She studies more than I do.

tips: Use comparative forms like “billigare”, “bättre”, “större”, and pair them with “än”.
Polite shopping questions often begin with “Har ni ...?” meaning “Do you have ...?” when talking to a shop assistant.

dialogues.title: Comparison, preference, and choosing between options

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Which apartment do you like more?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Den andra. Den är större och billigare.
lines.english: The second one. It is bigger and cheaper.

lines.speaker: A
lines.swedish: Men den första ligger närmare centrum.
lines.english: But the first one is closer to the center.

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Sant, men jag vill hellre ha mer plats.
lines.english: True, but I would rather have more space.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Can I help you?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Ja, jag vill köpa en tröja.
lines.english: Yes, I want to buy a sweater.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: What size?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Medium, thanks.

days.title: Housing ads and renting language
days.goal: Understand the main vocabulary in rental ads and simple housing talk.

vocabulary.exampleEnglish: The rent is 850 euros per month.
Do you need to pay a deposit?
The room is available from September.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Betalar du kontant eller med kort?
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: Are you paying cash or by card?

tips: Swedish often makes compact noun phrases in ads: “tvårumslägenhet”, “hyra per månad”, “möblerad bostad”.
Use “Hur mycket kostar det?” for “How much does it cost?” Swedish currency is kronor, often spoken as “kronor” or “spänn” informally.

lines.speaker: A
lines.swedish: Jag såg en annons för en möblerad lägenhet.
lines.english: I saw an ad for a furnished apartment.

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: How high is the rent?

lines.speaker: A
lines.swedish: Åttahundrafemtio euro och en månads deposition.
lines.english: Eight hundred and fifty euros and one month’s deposit.

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Låter rimligt om läget är bra.
lines.english: Sounds reasonable if the location is good.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: How much does the sweater cost?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: It costs three hundred kronor.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Okay, it is a little expensive.

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: The blue one is cheaper.

days.title: Moving, furniture, and practical home problems
days.goal: Handle simple conversations about moving and household problems.

vocabulary.exampleEnglish: We are going to move next month.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Soffan är för stor för rummet.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: The sofa is too big for the room.
Excuse me, can you help me?
I am looking for the station.
Can you show me the way?

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Ingen fara, jag kan hjälpa dig.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: No problem, I can help you.

tips: Use “måste” for necessity and “behöver” for need: “Jag måste flytta”, “Jag behöver en säng.”
A strong survival frame is “Kan du hjälpa mig?” meaning “Can you help me?” Add “ursäkta” first to sound polite.

dialogues.title: Moving, furniture, and practical home problems

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: When are you moving?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Nästa helg, men soffan är för stor.
lines.english: Next weekend, but the sofa is too big.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Do you need help?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Yes, and some tools.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Excuse me, can you help me?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Yes, of course.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: I am looking for the station.

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: I can show you the way.

days.title: Healthcare visits and appointment language
days.goal: Book, change, and discuss a healthcare appointment in more detail.

vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I want to book an appointment.
I need to change my appointment.
I am calling the health center.
The station is near the center.
The library is on the left.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Gå rakt fram i två minuter.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: Go straight ahead for two minutes.
The bus leaves from the stop called Glass.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Efter två korsningar ser du restaurangen.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: After two intersections you see the restaurant.

tips: Use “skulle vilja boka”, “behöver ändra”, and “kan komma” for polite service interaction.
Common direction phrases are “till höger” (to the right), “till vänster” (to the left), and “rakt fram” (straight ahead).

lines.speaker: Reception
lines.swedish: Vårdcentralen, hur kan jag hjälpa dig?
lines.english: Health center, how can I help you?

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.swedish: Jag skulle vilja boka en tid. Jag har haft feber sedan igår.
lines.english: I would like to book an appointment. I have had a fever since yesterday.

lines.speaker: Reception
lines.swedish: Kan du komma i morgon klockan nio?
lines.english: Can you come tomorrow at nine?

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.english: Yes, that works.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Where is the station?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Gå rakt fram och sväng till höger.
lines.english: Go straight ahead and turn right.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Is it far away?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: No, it is nearby.

days.title: Feelings, reactions, and everyday opinions
days.goal: Express emotions and simple opinions with more nuance.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Jag är lite orolig för provet.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I am a little worried about the test.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Jag är stolt över mina framsteg.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I am proud of my progress.
I felt relieved after the call.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Jag tycker att kursen är bra.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I think the course is good.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Det här är viktigt för mig.

vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I take the bus to work.

tips: Use “jag tycker att ...” for opinions and “jag känner mig ...” for emotions or temporary states.
To say how you travel, use “Jag åker ...” plus transport: “Jag åker buss.” “Jag åker tåg.”

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: How do you feel about the test?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: A little worried but also motivated.

lines.speaker: A
lines.swedish: Vad tycker du är viktigast att träna?
lines.english: What do you think is most important to practice?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: To speak longer without stopping.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: How do you get to town?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: I take the bus.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Do you have a ticket?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Yes, but the train departs soon.

days.title: Work tasks, schedules, and collaboration
days.goal: Describe job tasks, planning, and cooperation with others.

vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I am responsible for the report.
We have a deadline on Friday.
I try to remember the words.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Idag gör vi ett litet test.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: Today we do a small test.
Check that you understand the question.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Försök att svara snabbt men tydligt.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: Try to answer quickly but clearly.

tips: Use sequence words like “först”, “sedan”, and “till slut” to explain tasks clearly.
At this stage, fluency comes from recall speed. Short self-tests are more useful than rereading everything passively.

lines.speaker: A
lines.swedish: Vad ansvarar du för på jobbet?
lines.english: What are you responsible for at work?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Jag planerar möten och skriver rapporter.
lines.english: I plan meetings and write reports.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Do you work a lot with colleagues?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Yes, we collaborate every day.

lines.speaker: A
lines.swedish: Är du redo för ett litet test?
lines.english: Are you ready for a small test?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Yes, I am trying to remember everything.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: How do you get to work?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: I take the bus at eight.

days.title: Job search, CV basics, and applications
days.goal: Understand and produce simple Swedish related to jobs and applications.

vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I have experience in customer service.
I am looking for a full-time job.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Jag har en intervju på måndag.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I have an interview on Monday.
We are watching the film tonight.
I usually read in the evening.

tips: Formal Swedish often becomes more compact. Keep sentences clear and factual instead of overly complex.
Keep learning verbs as ready-to-use present forms first. Later you can study infinitives and verb classes in more detail.

dialogues.title: Job search, CV basics, and applications

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Have you sent your application?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Ja, och jag beskrev min erfarenhet tydligt.
lines.english: Yes, and I described my experience clearly.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Are you looking for full time or part time?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Preferably full time.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Do you walk to work?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: No, I come by bus.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Do you hear the teacher?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Ja, och jag ser tavlan också.
lines.english: Yes, and I see the board too.

days.title: School, courses, and learning discussions
days.goal: Discuss courses, assignments, deadlines, and learning plans.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Den här kursen hjälper mig mycket.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: This course helps me a lot.
The next submission is on Friday.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Jag läser varje morgon för att förstå mer.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I read every morning in order to understand more.

tips: With “för att”, you can explain purpose: “Jag studerar svenska för att klara provet.”
A strong beginner default is time or subject first, then the verb in second position: “Idag studerar jag svenska.” “Jag studerar svenska idag.”

lines.speaker: A
lines.swedish: Varför studerar du svenska så intensivt?
lines.english: Why are you studying Swedish so intensively?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: För att jag vill klara YKI-provet i augusti.
lines.english: Because I want to pass the YKI test in August.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: How often do you practice?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Six days a week.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: What are you doing today?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Today I work at home.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: And tomorrow?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Tomorrow I study Swedish.

days.title: Phone, internet, and digital problems
days.goal: Handle common digital-life issues in Swedish.

vocabulary.exampleEnglish: The internet is not working at home.
I use the app for tickets.
I have to update the phone.

tips: For technical problems, use “fungerar inte”, “kan inte”, and “måste” to explain the issue quickly.
Compare “Du bor här.” with “Bor du här?” For question-word questions, the question word comes first: “Var bor du?”

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Why did you not answer?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Min telefon fungerade inte och internet var nere.
lines.english: My phone was not working and the internet was down.

lines.speaker: A
lines.swedish: Har du provat att uppdatera appen?
lines.english: Have you tried updating the app?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Yes, now it works again.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Do you live in Stockholm?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: No, I live in Uppsala.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Why are you learning Swedish?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: För att jag vill jobba här.
lines.english: Because I want to work here.

days.title: Banking, payments, and everyday money
days.goal: Talk about paying, transferring, and everyday financial routines.

vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I must pay the bill today.
The money is in my account.
I do not like Anna either.

tips: Use “betala”, “överföra”, and “kostar” precisely, because small verb differences matter in service talk.
In simple statements, “inte” usually comes after the verb: “Jag bor inte här.” “Jag gillar inte kaffe.”

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: How do you want to pay?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: By card, thanks.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Have you also paid the rent?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Ja, jag överförde pengarna i morse.
lines.english: Yes, I transferred the money this morning.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Do you live here?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: No, I do not live here.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Do you have a ticket?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Nej, jag har ingen biljett ännu.
lines.english: No, I do not have a ticket yet.

days.title: Public services, forms, and identity details
days.goal: Understand basic public-service language and form-filling vocabulary.

vocabulary.exampleEnglish: Here is my personal identity number.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Jag måste fylla i en blankett.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I need to fill in a form.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Jag bor i en liten lägenhet.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I live in a small apartment.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Jag tycker att ett charmigt hus på landet är bättre.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I think a charming house in the countryside is better.

tips: Forms often use nouns instead of full sentences. Practice mapping those labels to real-life meaning.
At A1 level, start with common adjective chunks and pay attention to frequent forms in context rather than memorizing every agreement rule immediately.

dialogues.title: Public services, forms, and identity details

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Have you filled in the form?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Nästan, men jag saknar ett intyg.
lines.english: Almost, but I am missing a certificate.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Do not forget the signature.

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: No, I will not.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: What is your apartment like?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: It is small but nice.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Is the house new?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: No, the house is old.

days.title: Family logistics, childcare, and schedules
days.goal: Talk about family planning, childcare, and shared responsibilities.

vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I pick up the children at four.
She drops the child off at daycare.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Vi ansvarar för olika saker hemma.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: We are responsible for different things at home.
There was a schedule change today.
The room is a little messy today.

tips: Swedish often keeps the verb second even after time phrases: “På morgonen lämnar jag barnen.”
Short two-part descriptions are enough at A1 level: “Hon är snäll.” “Det är en fin bok.” Build confidence before adding complexity.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Can you pick up the children today?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Ja, men jag måste lämna dem tidigt i morgon.
lines.english: Yes, but I must drop them off early tomorrow.

lines.speaker: A
lines.swedish: Bra, då delar vi på det.
lines.english: Good, then we share it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Perfect.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: What is your teacher like?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: She is kind and funny.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Is Swedish difficult?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Ibland, men den är också fin.
lines.english: Sometimes, but it is also beautiful.

days.title: Travel planning, bookings, and accommodation
days.goal: Use Swedish for booking transport and accommodation.

vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I want to book a room.
The train’s departure is at seven.
We are going to stay overnight in Stockholm.
The book is on the table.
The keys are in the bag.
The cat sleeps under the chair.
The school is next to the library.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Butiken ligger mellan banken och kaféet.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: The shop is between the bank and the cafe.

tips: Questions about bookings often use “finns det”, “kan jag få”, and “skulle vilja boka”.
Start with a few high-frequency location words: på (on), i (in), under (under), bredvid (next to).

lines.speaker: A
lines.swedish: Jag skulle vilja boka ett enkelrum för två nätter.
lines.english: I would like to book a single room for two nights.

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: What date do you arrive?

lines.speaker: A
lines.swedish: Den tolfte juli, sent på kvällen.
lines.english: On the twelfth of July, late in the evening.

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: There is a room available.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Where is my book?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: It is on the table.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: And the keys?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: De är i väskan bredvid stolen.
lines.english: They are in the bag next to the chair.

days.title: Leisure events, plans, and recommendations
days.goal: Suggest activities and react to other people’s plans.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Det finns en ny utställning i stan.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: There is a new exhibition in town.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Vi går på konsert på fredag.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: We are going to a concert on Friday.
I can speak a little Swedish.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Jag orkar inte laga mat idag.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I do not have the energy to cook today.
I do not have time to come now.

tips: Use “vi kan ...”, “du borde ...”, and “ska vi ...?” for suggestions with different levels of force.
After a modal verb like “kan”, “vill”, or “måste”, the next verb stays in the infinitive: “Jag kan tala.” “Jag vill gå.”

lines.speaker: A
lines.swedish: Vad ska vi göra i helgen?
lines.english: What should we do this weekend?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Vi kan gå på en utställning eller en konsert.
lines.english: We can go to an exhibition or a concert.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: A concert sounds more fun.

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Bra, lördag passar bäst för mig.
lines.english: Good, Saturday works best for me.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Can you help me?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Ja, men jag måste gå snart.
lines.english: Yes, but I have to go soon.

lines.speaker: A
lines.swedish: Får jag fråga en sak först?
lines.english: May I ask one thing first?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Yes, of course.

days.title: Accidents, urgency, and emergency help
days.goal: Describe simple accidents and ask for urgent help.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Det har varit en liten olycka.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: There has been a small accident.
It is bleeding from the hand.
Do we need to call an ambulance?
I am going to study tonight.
We are going to cook this evening.
She is going to travel tomorrow.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Vad är din plan för helgen?
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: What is your plan for the weekend?
Next week I am going to travel.
I want to plan the weekend today.

tips: In urgent talk, simple present or past with clear facts is better than complex sentences.
A practical beginner future form is “ska” + infinitive: “Jag ska studera.” It often means “am going to.”

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: What has happened?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Han ramlade och nu blöder handen.
lines.english: He fell and now the hand is bleeding.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Should I call an ambulance?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Yes, please. It feels urgent.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: What are you going to do this evening?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: I am going to study Swedish.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: And tomorrow?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Imorgon ska jag träffa en vän.
lines.english: Tomorrow I am going to meet a friend.

days.title: Past tense stories and sequencing events
days.goal: Tell a short story about a past event in chronological order.

vocabulary.exampleEnglish: First I went to the station.
In the end I went home.
I am trying to write in Swedish.
I want to complain about the product.

tips: Sequence markers such as “först”, “sedan”, “efter det”, and “till slut” make imperfect grammar easier to follow.
Writing reveals gaps that speaking can hide. Keep your sentences short and correct rather than long and confusing.

dialogues.title: Past tense stories and sequencing events

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: How did the trip go yesterday?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Först missade jag bussen, sedan tog jag tåget.
lines.english: First I missed the bus, then I took the train.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: What happened after that?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Till slut kom jag fram i tid ändå.
lines.english: In the end I arrived on time anyway.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Can you write five sentences?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Yes, I am going to try.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Are they correct?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Inte alla, men jag lär mig.
lines.english: Not all of them, but I am learning.

days.title: Perfect tense and life experience
days.goal: Talk about experiences and actions connected to the present.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Jag har bott i Finland i tre år.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I have lived in Finland for three years.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Jag har inte gjort det ännu.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I have not done that yet.
I have already sent the email.
I need a can of tomato sauce.

tips: Perfect tense uses “har” + supine: “Jag har bott”, “Jag har arbetat”, “Jag har lärt mig”.
A practical pattern is “Var finns ...?” meaning “Where is ...?” Use it when you cannot find an item.

lines.speaker: A
lines.swedish: Hur länge har du bott i Finland?
lines.english: How long have you lived in Finland?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Jag har bott här i tre år.
lines.english: I have lived here for three years.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Have you already done the registration?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Ja, jag har redan skickat allt.
lines.english: Yes, I have already sent everything.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Excuse me, where is the milk?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Den finns längst bak i butiken.
lines.english: It is at the back of the store.

lines.speaker: A
lines.swedish: Tack. Kan jag få kvittot också?
lines.english: Thanks. Can I get the receipt too?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Yes, of course.

days.title: Future intentions, promises, and commitments
days.goal: Explain plans and intentions with stronger A2 control.

vocabulary.english: I intend / I am thinking of
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I intend to apply for the course.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Jag hoppas att det går bra.

vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I am ordering a main course.

tips: Combine future time with modal meaning: “Jag ska ...”, “Jag tänker ...”, “Jag hoppas att ...”.
At A1 level, short requests are fine: “Jag tar ...” or “Jag skulle vilja ha ...” both work in restaurants.

lines.speaker: A
lines.swedish: Hur tänker du förbereda dig för augusti?
lines.english: How are you planning to prepare for August?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Jag tänker studera varje morgon och göra mockprov varje vecka.
lines.english: I plan to study every morning and do mock tests every week.

lines.speaker: A
lines.swedish: Bra plan. När bestämmer du vilodagar?
lines.english: Good plan. When do you decide rest days?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: I keep Sundays free.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Do you have anything vegetarian?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Ja, vi har en vegetarisk huvudrätt.
lines.english: Yes, we have a vegetarian main course.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: What do you recommend?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: The soup is very popular.

days.title: Subordinate clauses and connectors
days.goal: Link ideas into longer A2 sentences with common connectors.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Jag stannade hemma eftersom jag var sjuk.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I stayed home because I was sick.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Om det regnar tar jag bussen.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: If it rains, I take the bus.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: När jag kommer hem lagar jag mat.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: When I come home I cook.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Jag gick ut fast det regnade.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I went out although it was raining.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Jag övar därför att jag behöver bättre flyt.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I practice because I need better fluency.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Jag tror att jag har feber.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I think I have a fever.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Jag kan inte träffas idag, jag har läkartid.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I cannot meet today, I have a doctor appointment.

tips: Practice “att”, “för att”, “när”, “om”, “eftersom”, and notice word order after subordinate clauses.
To describe pain, use “Jag har ont i ...” meaning “I have pain in ...” or “my ... hurts.”

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Why did you study at home yesterday?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Because the library was closed.

lines.speaker: A
lines.swedish: Vad gör du om du blir trött?
lines.english: What do you do if you get tired?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: När jag blir trött tar jag en kort paus.
lines.english: When I get tired I take a short break.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: What is the problem?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Jag har ont i huvudet och jag har feber.
lines.english: I have a headache and I have a fever.

lines.speaker: A
lines.swedish: Hur länge har du varit sjuk?
lines.english: How long have you been ill?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Since yesterday.

days.title: Reading notices, instructions, and warning signs
days.goal: Understand short practical texts quickly and accurately.

vocabulary.exampleEnglish: The library is closed on Sunday.
The shop is open until nine.
The offer is valid until Friday.
There is fog in the morning.

tips: Notices often omit subjects. Focus on key nouns, imperatives, dates, and conditions.
A common structure is “Det är ...” followed by the weather adjective or condition: “Det är kallt.” “Det regnar.”

dialogues.title: Reading notices, instructions, and warning signs

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: What does it say on the door?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Att kontoret är stängt efter klockan tre.
lines.english: That the office is closed after three o’clock.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: And the other sign?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: That registration only applies online.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: How is the weather today?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Det är soligt men lite kallt.
lines.english: It is sunny but a little cold.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Will it rain later?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Maybe this evening.

days.title: Email structure, polite requests, and replies
days.goal: Write clearer everyday emails for school, work, and services.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Vad ska jag skriva i ämnesraden?
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: What should I write in the subject line?

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Svara gärna så snart som möjligt.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: Please reply as soon as possible.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Hon tränar tre gånger i veckan.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: She exercises three times a week.
What do you do in your free time?
I usually have fika at the weekend.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Just nu är jag på semester med min mamma.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: Right now I am on holiday with my mother.

tips: Use simple openings and closings consistently: “Hej ...”, “Tack på förhand”, “Vänliga hälsningar”.
Many hobby sentences use the present tense: “Jag spelar ...” “Jag läser ...” “Jag tränar ...”. Keep them short.

dialogues.title: Email structure, polite requests, and replies

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: How do you begin the email?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Hi, I am writing because ...

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: And how do you finish?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Tack på förhand och vänliga hälsningar.
lines.english: Thanks in advance and kind regards.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: What do you do in your free time?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Jag gillar att läsa och träna.
lines.english: I like to read and exercise.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Do you also play music?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: A little, sometimes.

days.title: Rules, habits, and what people should do
days.goal: Talk about rules, expectations, and repeated behavior.

vocabulary.exampleEnglish: Do you want to have coffee tomorrow?

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Jag vill bjuda dig till min fest.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I want to invite you to my party.

tips: Use modal verbs like “måste”, “får”, “bör”, and “kan inte” to express obligation and permission.
A very useful pattern is “Vill du ...?” meaning “Do you want to ...?” Add a time or place after it.

dialogues.title: Rules, habits, and what people should do

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: What rules are there in the building?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Man måste vara tyst efter tio och man får inte röka inne.
lines.english: You must be quiet after ten and you may not smoke inside.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: That sounds reasonable.

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Yes, everyone must respect that.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Do you want to have coffee tomorrow?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Yes, gladly!

lines.speaker: A
lines.swedish: Ska vi träffas i stan klockan sex?
lines.english: Shall we meet in town at six?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: That works well.

days.title: Environment, recycling, and everyday sustainability
days.goal: Discuss simple environmental routines and recycling in Swedish.

vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I sort the garbage at home.
It is good for the environment.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Jag sparar vatten när jag duschar.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I save water when I shower.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Det låter bra, vi ses då.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: That sounds good, see you then.

tips: Use verbs like “sortera”, “återvinna”, and “spara” with clear objects for practical speech.
A simple declining structure is “Tyvärr, jag kan inte ...” meaning “Unfortunately, I cannot ...”.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: How do you recycle at home?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Vi sorterar plast, glas och papper.
lines.english: We sort plastic, glass, and paper.

lines.speaker: A
lines.swedish: Gör du något mer för miljön?
lines.english: Do you do anything else for the environment?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Yes, I try to save energy.

lines.speaker: A
lines.swedish: Vill du följa med på bio?
lines.english: Do you want to come to the cinema?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Unfortunately, I am busy this evening.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Okay, maybe another time.

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Yes, gladly next week.

days.title: News basics and short spoken summaries
days.goal: Understand and summarize the main point of simple news-like content.

vocabulary.exampleEnglish: It was an interesting news item.
The kitchen is small but nice.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Det finns en soffa i vardagsrummet.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: There is a sofa in the living room.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Jag bor i en liten lägenhet.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I live in a small apartment.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Lägenheten är på gångavstånd till affärer.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: The apartment is within walking distance of shops.
A balcony would also be good.

tips: Do not chase every word. Find topic, place, people, and result first.
Useful frames are “Jag bor i ...” and “Det finns ...” for describing what is in your home.

dialogues.title: News basics and short spoken summaries

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Did you understand the news item?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Inte allt, men jag förstod ämnet och resultatet.
lines.english: Not everything, but I understood the topic and the result.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Can you summarize briefly?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Ja, det handlade om kollektivtrafik i staden.
lines.english: Yes, it was about public transport in the city.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: What is your apartment like?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: It is small but cozy.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Do you have a big kitchen?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Nej, men jag har en fin soffa i vardagsrummet.
lines.english: No, but I have a nice sofa in the living room.

days.title: Problems, complaints, and customer-service talk
days.goal: Explain a problem and ask for a solution politely.

vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I do not want to complain, but ...

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Det är något fel med beställningen.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: There is something wrong with the order.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Jag har en bokning i mitt namn.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I have a booking in my name.
Is breakfast included in the price?

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Jag har en bokning i namnet Sharma.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I have a booking in the name Sharma.

tips: A useful complaint structure is: problem, evidence, request. Keep each step short and factual.
When asking for something in a hotel, short polite questions work well: “Har ni ...?” “Kan jag få ...?”

lines.speaker: Kund
lines.swedish: Hej, det är något fel med den här produkten.
lines.english: Hi, there is something wrong with this product.

lines.speaker: Personal
lines.english: What seems to be the problem?

lines.speaker: Kund
lines.swedish: Den fungerar inte och jag har kvittot kvar.
lines.english: It does not work and I still have the receipt.

lines.speaker: Personal
lines.swedish: Okej, vi kan byta den eller ge återbetalning.
lines.english: Okay, we can exchange it or give a refund.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Hello, I have a booking.

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Which name, please?

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Shool Dubey. Is breakfast included?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Ja, och här är din nyckel.
lines.english: Yes, and here is your key.

days.title: Longer speaking turns and discourse markers
days.goal: Speak for one to two minutes with clearer structure.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: För det första behöver jag mer tid.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: First of all I need more time.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Egentligen vill jag bo närmare jobbet.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: Actually I want to live closer to work.
I try to keep the conversation going.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Vi har ett kort samtal på svenska.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: We have a short conversation in Swedish.

tips: Use markers like “för det första”, “också”, “dessutom”, “men”, and “så” to hold the floor.
Use earlier chunks instead of searching for perfect grammar. A1 fluency grows from reliable phrases used often.

dialogues.title: Longer speaking turns and discourse markers

lines.speaker: A
lines.swedish: Hur kan du prata längre på provet?
lines.english: How can you speak longer in the test?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Jag använder enkla strukturer och några tydliga markörer.
lines.english: I use simple structures and a few clear markers.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Like which ones?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: För det första, dessutom, men, och till slut.
lines.english: First of all, in addition, but, and in the end.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Can we continue in Swedish?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Yes, but speak slowly.

lines.speaker: A
lines.swedish: Självklart. Vad gör du i helgen?
lines.english: Of course. What are you doing this weekend?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Jag ska träffa vänner och kanske resa lite.
lines.english: I am going to meet friends and maybe travel a little.

days.title: A2 review, production check, and B1 bridge
days.goal: Consolidate A2 and identify what must change to reach B1.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Jag behöver mer självständighet i språket.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I need more independence in the language.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Jag vill ha bättre flyt när jag talar.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I want better flow when I speak.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Jag tränar både flyt och noggrannhet.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I practice both fluency and accuracy.
I can see clear development now.
Last week I worked a lot.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Jag bodde i Spanien för ett år sedan.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I lived in Spain a year ago.

tips: At the end of A2, the priority is control of core structures under pressure, not rare grammar forms.
Start with common past forms as chunks, such as “var” (was) and “gjorde” (did). You do not need all Swedish past-tense rules yet.

dialogues.title: A2 review, production check, and B1 bridge

lines.speaker: A
lines.swedish: Vad är din största skillnad nu jämfört med A1?
lines.english: What is your biggest difference now compared with A1?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Jag kan förklara mer och skriva tydligare meddelanden.
lines.english: I can explain more and write clearer messages.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: What do you need for B1?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Mer flyt, längre svar och bättre strategier.
lines.english: More fluency, longer answers, and better strategies.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: What did you do yesterday?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Jag jobbade och sedan åt jag middag hemma.
lines.english: I worked and then I ate dinner at home.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Were you tired?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Yes, I was quite tired.

days.title: Society, citizenship, and civic vocabulary
days.goal: Build core vocabulary for society, citizenship, and participation.

vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I want to understand society better.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Jag bokade bord på en fin restaurang.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I booked a table at a nice restaurant.

tips: At B1, expand noun-based vocabulary but keep sentence structures simple and controlled.
Use time words like “först” (first) and “sedan” (then) to organize a simple story even if the grammar stays basic.

lines.speaker: A
lines.swedish: Varför är svenska viktigt för dig?
lines.english: Why is Swedish important to you?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: För att kunna delta mer aktivt i samhället.
lines.english: In order to participate more actively in society.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Are you also thinking about citizenship?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Ja, det är ett viktigt mål för mig.
lines.english: Yes, it is an important goal for me.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: How was your day yesterday?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Först jobbade jag, sedan lagade jag mat.
lines.english: First I worked, then I cooked.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: What did you do afterwards?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Efteråt såg jag en film och somnade tidigt.
lines.english: Afterwards I watched a film and fell asleep early.

words.swedish: att gå ut / att löpa ut

words.english: a law / according to the law

days.title: Background, migration, and personal journey
days.goal: Describe your life path, moves, and motivations in connected Swedish.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Jag flyttade till Finland för arbete.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I moved to Finland for work.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Det tar tid att anpassa sig.
Jag har fått mycket erfarenhet här.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: I have gained a lot of experience here.
I am going to travel next week.
We are going to eat soon.
I am going to call later.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Kanske kommer jag att skaffa nya vänner.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: Maybe I will get new friends.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Det kommer att bli roligt, hoppas jag.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: It will be fun, I hope.

tips: Mix perfect tense for lived experience with past tense for specific events when needed.
“Ska” is very common for planned future actions: “Jag ska resa nästa vecka.” Keep the following verb in the infinitive.

lines.speaker: A
lines.swedish: Kan du berätta lite om din bakgrund?
lines.english: Can you tell me a little about your background?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Jag kommer från Indien och flyttade till Finland för arbete.
lines.english: I come from India and moved to Finland for work.

lines.speaker: A
lines.swedish: Hur har det varit att anpassa sig?
lines.english: How has it been to adapt?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: Challenging but also educational.

lines.speaker: A
lines.swedish: Vad ska du göra nästa vecka?
lines.english: What are you going to do next week?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Jag ska resa och träffa familjen.
lines.english: I am going to travel and meet my family.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: When are you going to call them?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: I am going to call later today.

words.english: just the two of us, alone together

words.exampleEnglish: I was born in India.
I live in Helsinki now.

words.exampleSwedish: Jag var i dagvård i min hemstad.
words.exampleEnglish: I was in daycare in my home town.

words.exampleSwedish: Jag lekte med mina kusiner på gården.
words.exampleEnglish: I played with my cousins in the yard.

words.swedish: att fylla år + hur många år, när
words.exampleEnglish: I turn 35 in March.

words.swedish: att gå i skola + var, hur många år
words.english: to go to school + where, how many years
words.exampleSwedish: Jag gick i skola i nio år.
words.exampleEnglish: I went to school for nine years.

words.exampleSwedish: Jag började studera när jag var nitton.
words.exampleEnglish: I started studying when I was nineteen.
I have football as a hobby.
I studied computing at university.
I graduated from university in 2013.

words.exampleSwedish: Jag sökte till ett företag i Finland.
words.exampleEnglish: I applied to a company in Finland.

words.english: to get in / be accepted + where to
words.exampleEnglish: I got into the programme.

words.exampleSwedish: Jag fick ett jobb i Esbo.
words.exampleEnglish: I got a job in Espoo.
I work at an IT company.

words.exampleSwedish: Jag slutade på mitt gamla jobb.
words.exampleEnglish: I quit my old job.

words.exampleSwedish: Jag träffade min fru på jobbet.
words.exampleEnglish: I met my wife at work.

words.swedish: att bli kär / att bli förälskad + i vem
words.english: to fall in love + with whom
words.exampleSwedish: Jag blev kär i henne direkt.
words.exampleEnglish: I fell in love with her immediately.
We dated for two years.

vocabulary.exampleEnglish: That would be a good opportunity.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: I så fall behöver vi mer tid.
vocabulary.exampleEnglish: In that case we need more time.

tips: A practical B1 frame is “Om jag hade mer tid skulle jag ...”, but simpler “om ... så ...” answers are also fine.

lines.speaker: A

lines.speaker: A

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: I så fall skulle jag resa oftare.
lines.english: In that case I would travel more often.

days.title: Problem-case speaking simulation
days.goal: Handle a complex practical problem in a timed speaking task.

vocabulary.exampleSwedish: Hur kan vi lösa det här?

tips: Use a simple emergency framework: state the problem, explain why it matters, suggest options, choose one.

lines.speaker: A

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Att tiden är knapp och att vi saknar viktig information.
lines.english: That time is short and we lack important information.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: What alternatives are there?

lines.speaker: B
lines.swedish: Två realistiska alternativ, men jag föredrar det första.
lines.english: Two realistic alternatives, but I prefer the first.

lines.speaker: B

days.title: Integrated mock debrief and targeted repair
days.goal: Analyze recent mock performance and repair the patterns that still break under pressure.

prompt.sv: Ge komplimanger till din vän, t.ex. om hens stil.
prompt.en: Give your friend compliments, e.g. about their style.

lines.sv: Vilken snygg tröja! Den färgen passar dig verkligen bra.
lines.en: What a nice jumper! That colour really suits you.

lines.sv: Du har alltid så bra stil. Var har du köpt den?
lines.en: You always have such good style. Where did you buy it?

lines.sv: Du ser pigg ut idag. Har du klippt dig?
lines.en: You look fresh today. Have you had a haircut?

prompt.sv: Påminner husdjuret dig om sin ägare? Och påminner gifta par varandra?
prompt.en: Does the pet remind you of its owner? And do married couples resemble each other?

lines.sv: Ja, jag tycker faktiskt det. Många hundar liknar sina ägare, både till utseendet och personligheten.
lines.en: Yes, I actually think so. Many dogs resemble their owners, both in looks and in personality.

lines.sv: Gifta par börjar ofta likna varandra efter många år tillsammans.
lines.en: Married couples often start to resemble each other after many years together.

lines.sv: De använder samma ord och skrattar åt samma saker.
lines.en: They use the same words and laugh at the same things.

prompt.sv: Ett minne som är viktigt för dig. Vad hände då? Varför är det viktigt?
prompt.en: A memory that is important to you. What happened? Why is it important?

lines.sv: Ett viktigt minne för mig är dagen då jag flyttade till Finland.
lines.en: An important memory for me is the day I moved to Finland.

lines.sv: Det var i november och det var redan mörkt klockan fyra.
lines.en: It was in November and it was already dark at four o'clock.

lines.sv: Jag var både rädd och glad samtidigt.
lines.en: I was both scared and happy at the same time.

lines.sv: Det är viktigt för mig eftersom hela mitt liv förändrades den dagen.
lines.en: It is important to me because my whole life changed that day.

prompt.sv: Berätta om ditt första barndomsminne.
prompt.en: Tell about your first childhood memory.

lines.sv: Mitt första minne är från när jag var ungefär fyra år gammal.
lines.en: My first memory is from when I was about four years old.

lines.sv: Jag lekte i trädgården med min bror och det regnade.
lines.en: I was playing in the garden with my brother and it was raining.

lines.sv: Min mormor ropade att vi skulle komma in, men vi ville inte.
lines.en: My grandmother called us to come in, but we didn't want to.

lines.sv: Jag minns fortfarande lukten av den våta jorden.
lines.en: I still remember the smell of the wet earth.

prompt.sv: Problem i hemmet — kom på så många problem som möjligt som du måste ringa disponenten om.
prompt.en: Problems at home — think of as many problems as possible that you have to call the building manager about.

lines.sv: Kranen i köket läcker.
lines.en: The tap in the kitchen is leaking.

lines.sv: Avloppet i badrummet är igentäppt.
lines.en: The drain in the bathroom is blocked.

lines.sv: Elementen värmer inte, det är kallt i lägenheten.
lines.en: The radiators are not heating, it is cold in the apartment.

lines.sv: Ytterdörren till trapphuset går inte att låsa.
lines.en: The front door to the stairwell can't be locked.

lines.sv: Det luktar mögel i sovrummet.
lines.en: There is a smell of mould in the bedroom.

lines.sv: Grannen spelar hög musik varje natt.
lines.en: The neighbour plays loud music every night.

lines.speaker: Vän
lines.sv: Hej! Ursäkta att jag är lite sen. Det är fruktansvärt väder ute.
lines.en: Hi! Sorry I'm a bit late. The weather outside is terrible.

lines.speaker: DU
lines.sv: Ingen fara alls! Kom in, det är verkligen hemskt väder. Ta av dig jackan så hänger jag den här.
lines.en: No problem at all! Come in, the weather really is awful. Take off your jacket and I'll hang it here.

lines.speaker: Vän
lines.sv: Tack för inbjudan. Det var verkligen snällt av dig att bjuda in mig.
lines.en: Thanks for the invitation. It was really kind of you to invite me.

lines.speaker: DU
lines.hint: answer and offer something to drink
lines.sv: Det var så lite. Jag är glad att du kunde komma. Vad vill du ha att dricka — kaffe, te eller kanske ett glas vatten?
lines.en: Don't mention it. I'm glad you could come. What would you like to drink — coffee, tea or maybe a glass of water?

lines.speaker: Vän
lines.sv: Tack, jag skulle gärna ta en kopp kaffe om du har.
